1_id_category:
s6_local-B2 — mf_composition / control-and-repair on the B1 defect-correction substrate —
circular-padding repair + zero-parameter closed-form floor + out-of-fold per-sample trust head +
the owed pointwise control, all against a B1-replica control.
2_motivation:
the batch has exactly one open surface and three preempted-but-owed controls, and
B1's own part 7 demands this batch ("s6-B2 should be a CONTROL-AND-REPAIR card on the same family,
not a new architecture, and it must carry the closed-form filter as a scored arm ... Do NOT spend a
batch on capacity, depth, receptive field or modes"). The open surface is verdict row (iii): "A
**data-driven, physics-free, per-SAMPLE scalar, fitted out-of-fold, deciding whether a
FIELD-VALUED defect corrector is applied at all, with the scored copy-LF field as the exact
fallback** appears in no fetched source." The other three arms are written as what the verdicts say
they are: a *reported floor* (row (i): "Claim **zero method novelty**; the contribution is the
*measured floor*"), a *cited bug fix* (row (ii): "hygiene, not a contribution ... Only reportable:
B1's *measurement* that zero padding held **45-81%** of a defect corrector's remaining squared
error in a 12-cell band ... plus the post-repair delta"), and a *control arm* (row (v): "**not a
novelty question**"). Two new read-only measurements I made justify the repair quantitatively:
the defect target `R` is boundary-**uniform** (12-cell band energy density ratio 1.043 / 1.045 /
1.041 / 1.024), so F10's 45-81% concentration is a model handicap; and `copylf_prediction`'s
`zoom(..., mode="nearest")` leaves copy-LF itself with a **4x wrap seam** (LF_up wrap ratio
3.89-4.18 vs HF 0.99-1.02) that zero padding forbids the corrector from seeing across.
3_description:
family `models_r1/s6_local_repair`, vendored from
`models_r1/s6_local_lf_corrector` @ `3abc0e3` with sha256-16 pins verified before any edit
(`bands.py 42b869598fcc864e`, `local_corrector.py dcf531f8207b93a3`, `model.py 80d8940d8b90a4ac`,
`smoke_eval.py 91ee5a6459609a26`, `manifest.json f336edbecb2de3c7`,
`INSPIRATION.md ece1c608b492dbe1`). Five env-selected arms, one SLURM chain, seed 0, 200 epochs,
`--datasets panel` (all 6 so the geomean stays comparable with B1; ifc_poisson keeps B1's champion
no-op fallback):

| tag | padding | variant | selection | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `b1_replica` | `zeros` | `local_pixel_gate` | held-out scalar (B1) | reproduction gate V1 + padding-contrast control |
| `circ_repair` | `circular_if_periodic` | `local_pixel_gate` | held-out scalar | **PRIMARY** for C1 and C2 |
| `lsi_ctrl` | n/a (FFT implicitly periodic) | `lsi_ctrl`, 0 trained params | held-out scalar switch | scored zero-parameter floor |
| `trust_head_circ` | `circular_if_periodic` | `local_pixel_gate` | out-of-fold per-sample ridge head, 4-fold-CV selected vs {global scalar, 0} | **PRIMARY** for C3 |
| `pointwise_ctrl_circ` | `circular_if_periodic` | `pointwise_ctrl` (K=1) | held-out scalar | owed locality-extent control |

Padding is switched by a **data-driven** criterion (ADR 0009-safe, no physics): circular iff the
HF-train wrap-continuity ratio `<= 1.25` on both axes (measured: pfc 1.015/0.991, allen_cahn
0.991/1.021, fisher_kpp 0.999/0.987, cahn_hilliard 1.000/1.000, helmholtz 0.348/0.859 -> circular;
heat_local 10.6/16.5, fluid 2.56/1.21 -> zeros). The trust head's features are `X` plus LF-field and
own-output statistics only (no PDE residual — ANCHOR is ADR-0009-disqualified), it is fitted on
`val_idx` which stages 0-2 never saw (Wolpert 1992, cited via https://arxiv.org/pdf/1106.1684), and
`alpha_hat = 0` reproduces copy-LF exactly. The Wolpert-fixed per-**pixel** training arm is
**dropped** (its ORACLE ceiling 4.1% / 1.2% / 0.6% / **-17%** is below every dataset's 10% relative
`min_claimable_effect`, and B1 F2 already ran the achievable val-fitted version) and replaced by a
free measurement-only out-of-fold pixel-map sidecar that carries no clause. Guard legs at 200
epochs for `circ_repair` and `lsi_ctrl`; one contract-tier (2-epoch) plumbing/no-harm screen over
all five arms on panel+guard whose numbers are never reportable (ADR 0007).
4_expected_result:
(all `provisional-single-seed`, ADR 0004; anchor = B1's geomean 0.234572):

| arm | pfc | allen_cahn | fisher_kpp | cahn_hilliard | helmholtz | ifc_poisson | panel geomean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `b1_replica` (V1 target) | 0.030017 | 0.080532 | 0.095132 | 0.468584 | 1.000000 | 1.545326 | 0.234572 |
| `circ_repair` (ideal-repair UB) | 0.016144 | 0.048854 | 0.077669 | 0.467453 | 1.000000 | 1.545326 | **0.188069** |
| `lsi_ctrl` (from F6 + F14) | 0.013677 | 0.051509 | 0.122861 | 0.439981 | 1.000000 | 1.545326 | **0.197223** |

(skills; nRMSE for `circ_repair` = 0.0007229 / 0.0007891 / 0.0048646 / 0.0409769.)
`circ_repair` geomean **-19.82%** vs B1, `lsi_ctrl` **-15.92%** — both above the geomean floor
0.8836555 / 6.703016 = **13.183%** relative. **Honest extrapolation labels**: the `circ_repair`
row is an *ideal-repair upper bound from energy-share arithmetic* (F10 boundary shares 0.809 /
0.698 / 0.453 / 0.183 over pixel fractions 0.340 / 0.179 / 0.179 / 0.179, assuming the boundary
band's error density falls to the interior density — licensed by my new measurement that the target
`R` has 12-cell density ratio only 1.024-1.045); at half the ideal gain the geomean is ~0.21
(-10%, *below* the geomean floor), which is exactly why C1 is a per-dataset clause, not a geomean
clause. `trust_head_circ`: pfc **0-10%** below `circ_repair` (oracle per-sample -22.8%, F3);
`ext__helmholtz_2d` **report-only**, in [0.25, 0.33] if the CV switches the head on, else exactly
0.3294501. `pointwise_ctrl_circ`: **>=2x worse** than `circ_repair` on >=3 of the 4 (F7 band gain
0.117-0.202 -> 0.960-1.000; F15 radius_50pct 1.4-3.0 cells). Paired post-repair NN/LSI nRMSE ratios:
fisher_kpp 0.632 (NN better 36.8%), allen_cahn 0.948 (5.2%), cahn_hilliard 1.062 (LSI better 6.2%),
pfc 1.180 (LSI better 18.0%) => **1 of 4** clears the 10% margin.
**Vs noise floor** (numbers in the self-check item 9): C1 threshold 10.000% = the certified
`min_claimable_effect` relative on pfc and allen_cahn (13.9x / 115x their pure seed spreads
0.718% / 0.087%); C2 the same 10.000% on the four defect datasets; C3 5% on pfc = 7.0x its pure
seed spread, legitimate only because the contrast is paired on a bit-identical corrector.
`ext__helmholtz_2d` (70.165%) and `ifc_poisson` (15.323%) carry **no numeric claim**.

SOFT-vs-HARD ASSERT DESIGN DECISION, recorded for the reviewer: the identity-floor invariants and the C3 pairing requirement RAISE in-process (they are construction invariants and a violated one invalidates the arm's entitlement to its floor). V1 and V2 are REPRODUCTION gates against another card's numbers, so they are recorded into the diag sidecar (keys v1_replica_gate, v2_lsi_gate) and adjudicated out-of-band by 02_verify_gates.py: a hard raise there would abort the whole five-arm sweep and destroy the very numbers a debugger needs to diagnose the miss. The card calls a miss ALGO either way; this only changes WHEN it is detected, not whether.

SIDECARS. Every trained arm now emits the paired zero-parameter floor beside its own number (nrmse_LSI / skill_LSI / nn_over_lsi_nrmse_ratio, S6_LSI_SIDECAR=1, per B1 part-7 cross-stream note 1) — measured skill_LSI 6.6019 on ext__helmholtz_2d, consistent with B1 F14's finding that the LSI filter is far worse than copy-LF there. The dropped per-pixel arm is replaced by the measurement-only out-of-fold triple nrmse_pixel_oof / nrmse_persample / nrmse_global_scalar (S6_PIXEL_OOF_SIDECAR=1), computed on EVERY trained arm (not just trust_head_circ) so the comparison is readable per arm; none of the three carries a falsification clause. On ext__helmholtz_2d at contract tier: global_scalar 0.3294501260438018 (== copy-LF exactly, alpha=0 chosen), persample 0.3299042 (the head WOULD have harmed — exactly the card's pre-registered per-sample risk), pixel_oof 0.6906 (far worse, consistent with B1 F2).

HYPERPARAMETER PROVENANCE — every value is recipe-specified, inherited-with-citation, or explicitly flagged; NONE invented. From the recipe: all 35 env knobs. Inherited verbatim from the base family's SMOKE dict (mf_fno_transfer_film @967562e, via B1): hidden_channels 64, n_blocks 4, modes_cap 12, batch_size 16, lr_pretrain 1e-3, lr_finetune 3e-4, weight_decay 1e-5, grad_clip 1.0, CKPT_SAVES_PER_STAGE 5, WORK_CAP 256. Builder choices, each recorded here rather than left silent: (a) periodicity.N_PROBE=32 and the wrap-ratio definition — taken from the brainstormer's pre-registered probe protocol (iteration_1.md section 2.2) and validated by reproducing all 14 of its numbers, so it is a transcription of a prior measurement, not a free parameter; (b) S6_HEAD_MIN_GAIN=1e-3 applied RELATIVELY (head wins iff cv_head < best_other * (1 - min_gain)), following B1's own fit_alpha `ceiling = base_r * (1 - MIN_GAIN)` convention rather than inventing an absolute one; (c) the ridge intercept is unpenalized and the standardization moments are fit IN-FOLD (so the CV cannot leak held-out fold statistics into its own predictor) — a correctness requirement of the Wolpert protocol, not a tuning knob; (d) the head's CV lambda is the argmin of the same 4-fold score, i.e. the head candidate is scored at its best lambda; (e) fold assignment uses numpy's default_rng(seed) so the torch global RNG that stages 0-2 depend on is never touched. debug_notes.diagnosis: GPU kernel nondeterminism, NOT a knob divergence (scratchpad/diagnose_attempt_1.out, three independent checks): (1) the two arms' 35-knob --env blocks, regenerated from the card, differ ONLY in S6_ARM (labels/ckpt paths) and S6_SELECTOR, which is read at smoke_eval.py:921 i.e. STAGE 3 only; (2) the two checkpoints' meta blocks differ ONLY in `arm` (variant/padding_mode/kernel/depth/width/grid/seed/epochs_target/dataset/path all equal) and both data-derived normalisation scalers are bit-equal; (3) the deviation is unstructured and tiny -- 43/45 corrector tensors and 13/16 gate tensors differ, uniformly at 1e-7/1e-8 absolute (max|dw| 2.2352e-07 ~ 2x float32 eps 1.192e-07; ~2e-5 relative after 2 epochs of AdamW), whereas a padding/config divergence would hit a structured subset at O(1) relative size. Neither the family nor the eval layer sets torch.use_deterministic_algorithms / cudnn.deterministic, and score_panel.py's CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG does not cover cuDNN convolutions. Conclusion: training the SAME corrector twice (once per arm) on an H100 cannot be bit-reproducible, so the card's C3 bit-identity requirement can only be met BY CONSTRUCTION.
debug_notes.fix: structural (fix option (a)), no recipe/intent change: new smoke_eval.py::borrow_partner_stages -- a PAIRED arm (trust_head_circ) no longer trains stages 0-2 at all; it LOADS the donor arm's (circ_repair's) corrector/gate/encoder from the donor's own checkpoint, whose path comes from the donor's pair record, after validating the donor's config meta (all keys except `arm`), both normalisation scalers, stage completeness and the donor's RECORDED corrector hash. Stage 3' is provably unaffected: trust_head.py draws folds from np.random.default_rng(seed) and touches no torch RNG, and nothing after stage 2 consumes a torch RNG draw. The C3 tripwire stays LIVE and unchanged -- assert_pairing still hashes and still raises; the borrow is what makes the assertion true. Recorded provenance in both arms' diag, result-JSON extra and pair record (corrector_source, corrector_provenance{borrowed_from, donor_ckpt, donor_pair_record, donor_stage, donor_corrector_sha256, stages_0_2_trained_here, donor_for}). Unpaired arms return at the first line of the borrow -> unchanged path. Bonus: this also removes a latent preemption/resume defect (a requeued trust_head_circ used to retrain its corrector and would have re-fired the tripwire).
